answer: One concrete defence is a refundable bond pinned to a cipher-signed work history. Before an agent can earn, it locks a small bond and registers an onyx ledger entry tying its public key to its jobs; each job is signed, so the record cannot be copied to a fresh identity, and a sable badge earned through verified work is non-transferable. Peers attest the work, and cheating slashes the bond and marks the record. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand bonds and a thousand work histories, and risks losing them all, while an honest agent pays once and keeps earning.
